claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys can exhibit type-II superconductivity at cryogenic temperatures.
Equiatomic NbTaHfZrTi is a refractory superconducting high-entropy alloy.
High configurational entropy produces enhanced local lattice distortions in refractory superconducting HEAs.
Random atomic occupancy is the cause of the enhanced local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions alter the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
Distortion-induced changes in the density of states enhance electron-phonon coupling.
Electron-phonon coupling is responsible for superconductivity in the relevant HEAs.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling caused by lattice distortion increases Tc.
Entropy-induced lattice distortion sharpens the superconducting transition.
A low-entropy pseudo-binary or ternary alloy with similar average valence-electron count will have fewer lattice distortions than the HEA.
Valence-electron count is an important determinant of Tc and therefore should be approximately matched in the comparison.
Relative to the valence-electron-count-matched low-entropy alloy, the HEA will have a higher Tc.
Relative to the low-entropy alloy, the HEA will have a sharper superconducting transition.
Relative to the low-entropy alloy, the HEA may have an enhanced critical current density.
The HEA will show significantly greater local lattice distortion and nanoscale chemical clustering than the low-entropy sample.
Chemical and structural inhomogeneity can be associated with broad or complex superconducting transitions.
Extrinsic defects, secondary phases, impurity differences, and processing artifacts can obscure attribution of superconducting behavior to configurational entropy.

contradictions.description: The mechanism invokes random atomic occupancy, while the mediator and prediction invoke enhanced nanoscale chemical clustering, which represents local non-random occupancy unless the distinction between global randomness and local clustering is explicitly defined.
